prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean Liberty, Missouri (the city north of Kansas City)? I can either (A) look up local certified backflow testers and give names/phone numbers, or (B) give quick instructions so you can find and vet testers yourself. I can’t browse the web unless you want me to try to pull current local listings — let me know.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick, useful checklist and places to check right away:

Who normally does backflow testing and repair
- Licensed plumbers who are certified backflow assembly testers
- Irrigation/sprinkler companies with certified testers
- Fire-protection contractors (for fire‑line assemblies)
- Some utility/water departments maintain an approved tester list or can recommend contractors

Where to check for local, certified testers
- City of Liberty / Liberty Utilities (water department) — they often keep a list of approved or previously used vendors and can tell you local requirements for reporting tests.
- Clay County or Kansas City water utility websites (if your property is served by a different utility)
- Missouri backflow tester certification registry or the agency that issues tester certifications (look for “Backflow Assembly Tester” in Missouri)
- Online directories: Google Maps, Angi, HomeAdvisor, or Yelp (filter for “backflow testing” + “Liberty MO”)

What to ask and verify before hiring
- Are you a certified backflow assembly tester? What’s your certification number/agency?
- Are you licensed and insured? (ask for proof)
- Do you provide a written test report (AWWA/ASSE format) and tag the device after testing?
- Will you pull permits or notify the water utility if required?
- Estimated price for testing and for common repairs (and parts warranties)
- Availability for emergency repair / turnaround for re‑test if repairs are needed

Typical costs (ballpark)
- Annual test: roughly $50–$150 per device (varies by region and device type)
- Simple repairs/parts: $50–$300
- Major repairs or assembly replacement: several hundred to over $1,000, depending on device type (RPZ, double check, etc.)

Sample short script to call/email a contractor
“Hi — I need annual backflow testing (and possibly repair) for an [RPZ/double-check/pressure vacuum breaker] at my property in Liberty, MO (ZIP ___). Are you a certified backflow assembly tester in Missouri? What is your test fee, do you provide a written report and tag, and are you insured? Can you come out on [date range]?”

If you want, tell me your address or ZIP code and whether this is residential or commercial and I’ll try to pull a short list of nearby certified testers and contact info.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
